name: Terrorist Content Online Regulation
evidence_rating: thin: Commission activity counts and a qualitative rights assessment; no measure of effect on terrorist content or on platforms
summary: Since June 2022 national authorities can order platforms to remove terrorist content within one hour. The Commission counted about 350 such orders by end-2023, mostly acted on quickly, and judged the law a success, but no study measures whether terrorist content online actually fell. The EU's rights agency (2026) warns of over-removal and uneven effects on Muslim and Arabic-speaking users.

indicators.objective: The proposal has no LFS indicators; the memorandum committed the Commission to a monitoring programme within one year, an implementation report after two years and an evaluation (Article 23)

indicators.indicator: Faster removal: removal orders executed within one hour
indicators.evidence: At least 349 removal orders issued by six Member States by end-2023 (to Telegram, Meta, X, TikTok, Archive.org and others), mostly with swift follow-up; Commission judges impact 'positive'. No measure of overall prevalence of terrorist content.

indicators.indicator: Competent authorities designated; cooperation via Europol (PERCI)
indicators.evidence: 23 Member States had designated authorities by end-2023 after infringement procedures against 22; 14,615 referrals processed in PERCI July-Dec 2023.

indicators.objective: Safeguards against erroneous removal / fundamental rights
indicators.indicator: Complaints, reinstatements and court challenges; no over-removal
indicators.evidence: No removal order scrutinised, reinstated or challenged in court by end-2023. FRA (2026) interviews flag risk of over-removal and disproportionate effects on Muslims and Arabic speakers. No quantitative evidence.

indicators.indicator: Less fragmentation and lower compliance costs for hosting providers

literature.citation: European Commission (2018), Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on preventing the dissemination of terrorist content online (executive summary SWD(2018) 409), SWD(2018) 408
literature.title: Impact Assessment accompanying the proposal on preventing the dissemination of terrorist content online (executive summary SWD(2018) 409)
literature.outcomes: removal speed; transparency; fundamental rights; compliance costs
literature.headline: Preferred option (one-hour removal orders, referrals, proactive measures for exposed providers, safeguards, transparency) judged most effective, with highest costs and highest benefits; no quantified headline
literature.summary_plain: The Commission expected binding one-hour removal orders and transparency duties to cut the spread of terrorist propaganda online, and accepted higher costs for platforms.

literature.citation: European Commission (2024), Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 on addressing the dissemination of terrorist content online (with SWD(2024) 36), COM(2024) 64
literature.title: Report on the implementation of Regulation (EU) 2021/784 on addressing the dissemination of terrorist content online (with SWD(2024) 36)
literature.method: implementation report (Member State, Europol and provider data)
literature.headline: By 31 Dec 2023: 349+ removal orders from six Member States, mostly executed quickly; 23 Member States designated authorities; 14,615 referrals via PERCI; no orders challenged; Commission concludes a positive impact in limiting spread of terrorist content
literature.summary_plain: The Commission's first report counts about 350 removal orders in 2023, mostly acted on quickly, and calls the law a success - but the evidence is activity counts, not a measured drop in terrorist content.

literature.citation: EU Agency for Fundamental Rights (FRA) (2026), Regulating online terrorist content - Balancing public safety and fundamental rights, FRA report, 22 January 2026
literature.title: Regulating online terrorist content - Balancing public safety and fundamental rights
literature.method: qualitative (fieldwork interviews with 62 practitioners and experts)
literature.headline: Moderation by authorities and platforms may disproportionately affect Muslims and Arabic speakers while far-right content gets less scrutiny; risks of over-removal and chilling of free expression; recommends clearer definitions, transparency and avoiding incentives to over-remove
literature.summary_plain: The EU's rights agency warns that the terrorist content rules may lead platforms to over-remove legal posts and hit Muslim and Arabic-speaking users hardest, based on interviews with experts.

literature.title: Transparency Report as per Article 8 of the Terrorist Content Online Regulation and Monitoring Report as per Article 21(1) - Year under review 2025
literature.method: administrative statistics on removal orders, removal requests, objections and Article 5 procedures
literature.outcomes: removal orders issued and complied with, removal requests, compliance rates
literature.headline: In 2025 the Bundeskriminalamt issued 245 removal orders (99.2% implemented, 237 fewer than in 2024) and 29,792 voluntary removal requests (93.2% implemented vs 87.4% in 2024).
literature.summary_plain: Germany's police used the regulation's binding one-hour removal orders a few hundred times in 2025 and platforms almost always complied, while far more content was taken down through voluntary requests.
literature.quality: Official counts from the competent authority; outputs only, no measure of effect on terrorist content availability
literature.interested_party: National competent authority reporting on its own activity
literature.citation: Bundesnetzagentur (with Bundeskriminalamt data) (2026), Transparency Report as per Article 8 of the Terrorist Content Online Regulation and Monitoring Report as per Article 21(1) - Year under review 2025, Bundesnetzagentur, Germany, March 2026

literature.authors: WODC (Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek- en Datacentrum, Dutch Ministry of Justice and Security); external research team (Rotterdam) not named in summary
literature.title: Evaluation of Implementation Act on the Regulation on Terrorist Content Online - Final report (English summary)
literature.method: statutory ex-post evaluation: document review, 28 semi-structured interviews, workshops, case studies of Germany, Ireland and Sweden, plus removal-order statistics
literature.outcomes: removal orders issued and complied with; over-removal; administrative burden; governance; effect on terrorist content online
literature.headline: About 330 removal orders were issued by the Dutch authority (ATKM) in 2024-2025, almost all complied with within the one-hour deadline (around 20% of all EU removal orders), with no fines, appeals or exposure decisions; but about three-quarters of flagged content falls outside scope and no effect on overall terrorist content can be shown.
literature.summary_plain: A Dutch government-commissioned evaluation found that when the Dutch authority orders a platform to remove terrorist content, it is almost always taken down within an hour and there is no sign of lawful content being removed by mistake. But it cannot show that the law has reduced terrorist content online overall, partly because there was no baseline and content moves to closed channels.
literature.period_geography: Sept 2023 - June 2026; Netherlands (with comparisons to DE, IE, SE)
literature.quality: Mixed-methods implementation evaluation; no baseline or counterfactual for impact; only the English summary was read.
literature.interested_party: Commissioned by the ministry responsible for the implementing act
literature.citation: WODC (Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek- en Datacentrum, Dutch Ministry of Justice and Security); external research team (Rotterdam) not named in summary (2026), Evaluation of Implementation Act on the Regulation on Terrorist Content Online - Final report (English summary), WODC evaluation report (28 July 2026)

literature.title: Terrorist Content Online Regulation Transparency Report 2025 (Article 8 transparency report and Article 21(1) monitoring report)
literature.venue: An Garda Síochána report (year under review 2025, as of March 2026)
literature.method: statutory statistical transparency report of the Irish competent authority
literature.outcomes: removal orders issued, scrutinised and implemented
literature.headline: Ireland's competent authority issued one removal order in 2025, and the content was taken down; no removal orders were scrutinised under Article 4.
literature.summary_plain: Ireland hosts the EU headquarters of many big platforms, yet its police issued only one order under the EU terrorist-content law in 2025, which was obeyed.
literature.quality: Bare counts only; shows very low use of removal orders by the authority in the main hosting jurisdiction.
literature.citation: An Garda Síochána (2026), Terrorist Content Online Regulation Transparency Report 2025 (Article 8 transparency report and Article 21(1) monitoring report), An Garda Síochána report (year under review 2025, as of March 2026)
